transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… mostly my sleep. It’s gotten really unreliable. I’ll go to bed completely exhausted, like after a full day of sales meetings and forecasts and all that, and then I’m just lying there replaying numbers, team issues, things I need to fix. And if I do fall asleep, I’m waking up around 3 or 4 and my brain just won’t shut off again. It’s starting to feel like I can’t count on sleeping normally anymore.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things other than work when you're lying awake at night?

Yeah… it’s not just work, though work is kind of the starting point. Like, my mind will go from whether we’re going to hit the launch numbers, to whether someone on my team is unhappy and might quit, and then somehow I’m thinking about the mortgage, or a client renewal, or—honestly even a small email delay starts feeling like it could turn into a huge problem.  

And then I’ll remember something random, like a neighbor mentioning repairs on their house, and suddenly I’m doing math in my head about our finances. So yes, I guess it jumps around a lot.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain activities or situations because of your worries?

I’m not sure I’d say I’m avoiding things, exactly. I mean… I still go to work, I still take calls and handle meetings. Sometimes I’ll put off opening an email if I have a bad feeling about it, but then I end up checking it anyway.

It’s hard to tell what counts as avoiding. Like last weekend I almost didn’t go to this dinner because I was thinking about everything I needed to do, but also I was just tired, and my friend had picked this loud restaurant downtown where parking is impossible, so… I don’t know. Maybe a little, but I haven’t really noticed a clear pattern.
Have you been experiencing any physical symptoms like headaches or stomach issues when you're feeling anxious or overwhelmed?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I haven’t tracked it that closely. Sometimes I’ll feel kind of… off when I’m overwhelmed, but I don’t know if I’d call it headaches or stomach issues specifically.

It’s funny, because at work people always say stress “goes to their stomach,” and I’ll be sitting there in a meeting thinking, am I supposed to notice that? But then I’m also trying to listen to someone talk about quarterly numbers, and then my phone buzzes, and I lose the thread completely. So… I guess I haven’t noticed a clear pattern with physical stuff.
Has something traumatic happened to you recently?

Not that I can think of. I mean, nothing like… a major accident or anything. Recent is a little hard because everything lately feels kind of piled up, but I wouldn’t call any one thing traumatic.

I did get really shaken up by a conversation with my boss a few weeks ago, but that’s not really what you mean, probably. I just keep replaying things like that. But no, I don’t think something traumatic happened recently.
Do you ever experience memories or images that feel like they're intruding into your thoughts, making you relive a moment over and over?

I don’t think so… not in the way you mean, like reliving something. I do replay conversations a lot, like if I said something weird in a meeting, I’ll go over it again later while I’m making dinner or trying to watch TV, and then I end up not even following the show.

But that feels more like thinking too much, not like an image forcing its way in. I mean, unless that counts? I guess I don’t really have a specific moment that comes back like that.
Do you find that you're staying away from social gatherings or events because of your worries?

I don’t know if I’d say I’m staying away from them exactly. I mean, sometimes I think about not going because I’m already tired from work, or because it feels like there’s going to be all this small talk, and then I start thinking about what I’m supposed to wear or whether I’ll be awkward.

But then other times I do go and it’s fine, or at least fine enough. It depends on the event, I guess. Like a big work thing feels different than dinner with people I already know. Sorry, I’m kind of circling it—I'm not sure I’ve noticed a clear pattern of avoiding social stuff because of worry.
Do you have nightmares that wake you up or disturb your sleep?

Not really nightmares, no. I mean, I wake up disturbed, but it’s more like… I go to bed exhausted and then my brain starts going through forecasts, team issues, what I missed, what I’m going to have to fix tomorrow.

And then I’ll wake up at like 3 or 4 in the morning and it’s the same thing, like my brain just picks up where it left off and won’t power down. So it’s not usually a scary dream waking me up—more just the thinking, I guess.
Have you noticed your worries or lack of sleep affecting your relationships with family or friends?

Yeah… I think it has, more than I wanted to admit. Like at work, during pipeline reviews, I’ll get stuck second-guessing decisions or worrying I missed something, and then the whole meeting gets tense because I’m not just moving through it normally.

And then by the time I get home, I’m just… used up. My husband will be talking to me and I’ll realize I’m only half listening, or I’ll snap over something small. Which is stupid, because I don’t mean to take it home with me. I used to be better at switching gears, I think.
Is there something specific that you think is causing your sleep to be unreliable?

I think it’s work, mostly. Or not even work exactly, but the stuff around it—forecasts, whether I handled something with my team the right way, what I missed, what’s going to blow up the next day.

I’ll be completely exhausted and think I should just fall asleep, but then I’m lying there replaying things. And then if I wake up around 3 or 4, it’s like my brain just starts the whole checklist again and I can’t get it to shut off. So yeah, I think that’s the main thing making my sleep so unreliable.
Do you find yourself consistently avoiding specific tasks or situations at work because of your worries?

I don’t know if I’d say I’m consistently avoiding things. I mean, I procrastinate sometimes, but I’m not sure if that’s the same as avoiding. Like, I’ll put off opening a report or responding to something if I’m worried it’s going to turn into a whole thing.

But then sometimes it’s just because the day gets away from me—there are so many little fires, and then Slack messages, and then someone needs something, and suddenly it’s 5:30 and I’ve been meaning to do the one thing all day. So… I guess I’m not sure. I don’t think there’s one specific task I’m avoiding all the time.
Is there a particular work-related issue that you think is most responsible for your sleep problems?

Probably the forecasts. I mean, that’s the thing I keep coming back to at night—whether the numbers are right, whether I missed something obvious, whether someone on my team is struggling and I didn’t handle it the right way.

It’s weird because I’ll go to bed completely exhausted, like I can barely keep my eyes open, and then as soon as it’s quiet my brain starts replaying everything. And then if I wake up at 3 or 4, it’s like… there it is again. Forecasts, team issues, what I need to fix tomorrow. I can’t get it to power down.

Sorry, that’s probably a long way of saying yes—work stuff, especially forecasts and team problems, seems like the main thing.
Has your sleep become unreliable since a particular stressful event at work, like the conversation with your boss a few weeks ago?

Not really that one conversation, no. I mean, it didn’t help, and I definitely replayed it afterward, but the sleep thing was already happening before that.

I think it’s been building since the sales division reorganization… about thirteen months ago, I guess. That’s when everything started feeling less predictable. New structure, different expectations, people shifting around—sorry, I know that’s not exactly what you asked. But yeah, it wasn’t just a few weeks ago. It’s been kind of accumulating since then.
Do you think your sleep problems and worries started as a direct reaction to the changes at work, like the sales division reorganization?

Yeah, I think so… not like it happened overnight, but that’s when it started to build. The reorganization was about thirteen months ago, and since then it’s just felt like one thing after another.

I remember at first thinking, okay, everyone’s just adjusting, it’ll settle down. And then it didn’t really settle. Or maybe I didn’t settle. Sorry, I’m kind of circling around it—but yes, I’d say the sleep problems and worrying have been building since that change at work.
Do you think your worries and sleep problems would improve if the work situation or the things that are worrying you were to resolve?

I want to say yes, because that sounds logical—like if the work stuff calmed down, I’d sleep better. And maybe I would, a little.

But honestly, I don’t know if it would fully stop. I can tell myself, “Brenda, you’ve done the plan, let it go,” and for a minute I’ll believe it. Then five minutes later I’m back in another loop. I’ll check one concern off, and then three more pop up—like, okay, the forecast is handled, but what about that client email, or whether I said the wrong thing in the meeting, or… I don’t know, something else.

Sorry, I’m wandering. I guess I’m saying even when one thing resolves, my brain just seems to find the next thing to worry about.
Do you think your worries and sleep problems are a direct reaction to the stress at work, or are they more about your general tendency to worry about many things?

I think it’s both, but… more the second one, if I’m being honest. Work may have kicked it up, but my mind doesn’t stay only on work.

Most days it jumps around—like, are we going to hit the launch numbers, is someone on my team unhappy enough to quit, then suddenly I’m thinking about the mortgage, or whether a client is going to renew. And then if there’s a tiny delay, like someone doesn’t respond to an email, I start turning it into this whole bigger thing in my head.

Sorry, I’m probably over-explaining. I guess it feels less like one work stressor and more like my brain is always looking for the next thing to worry about.
Do you worry about things outside of work, like your health, relationships, or finances, as much as you worry about work-related issues?

Yes, I do. I mean, work is the big one because it’s right in front of me all day, but it doesn’t stay there.

Most days my mind jumps from, you know, are we going to hit the launch numbers, to whether someone on my team is about to quit, and then somehow I’m thinking about the mortgage or whether a client is going to renew. And then if there’s a small delay—like an email doesn’t come back quickly—I start thinking, oh no, this could turn into something major.

So… yes, it’s not just work. It kind of spreads into everything.
Do you worry about things outside of work, such as your health or relationships, to the same extent as you worry about work-related issues?

Yeah… I think it’s pretty much the same, even if work is the easiest thing to point to.

Like most days my mind will go from, are we going to hit the launch numbers, to, oh god, is someone on my team about to quit, and then I’m suddenly thinking about the mortgage or whether a client is going to renew. And then if there’s some tiny delay—like someone doesn’t answer right away—I start making it into this whole big thing in my head.

Sorry, I know you asked about outside work. I guess the answer is yes, it spreads beyond work.
Do you think your worrying would stop if all the stressors in your life, including those outside of work, were completely resolved?

I don’t think it would completely stop, no. I mean, it might get quieter for a bit if everything was magically resolved, but my brain would probably just find the next thing.

Most days it jumps around anyway—like, will we hit the launch numbers, is someone on my team about to quit, then I’m thinking about the mortgage or whether a client will renew. And if there’s some tiny delay, like an email taking too long, I start treating it like it could become something major.

Sorry, I know that’s not exactly a clean answer. I guess I’m saying the stressors matter, but the worrying feels like it has its own momentum.
How long have you been experiencing excessive worry about a variety of things, not just limited to work?

Um… I’d say it’s been building for about thirteen months now. It really seemed to start around the sales division reorganization.

I remember that period because everything felt like it got shuffled at once—new reporting lines, people acting weird about where they’d land, and I kept thinking I should be handling it better. But yeah, if you’re asking how long it’s been more than just normal stress… about thirteen months.
